title: Metal Wire Structure — Wire Tree Sculpture
body: Public edition. Public craft reference. A wire tree with a trunk and branching limbs. Materials: aluminum sculpting wire 12-gauge (3 mm) for the trunk, 16-gauge for branches, wire cutters, round-nose pliers, a wooden base with a drilled hole. Steps: (1) cut 12 trunk wires twice the finished tree height; (2) twist them together from the base upward, leaving the top third loose; (3) divide loose ends into branch groups of 2-3 and twist each; (4) split branch ends into twigs; (5) curl twig tips with round-nose pliers; (6) splay the base wires into roots and anchor into the base. Tip: twist in one direction only — reversing kinks the wire.

title: Metal Wire Structure — Wire Figure Armature
body: Public edition. Public craft reference. A poseable human armature for sculpting. Materials: 12-gauge aluminum wire, 16-gauge wire, pliers, cutters. Steps: (1) cut one spine wire head-to-hip and one hip-to-foot per leg; (2) twist the pelvis block where they cross; (3) add arm wires at the shoulder line; (4) wrap joints with 16-gauge wire to lock them; (5) pose and check balance on both feet. Proportions: total height about 7.5 heads. Tip: wrap joints tight — loose joints drift while you sculpt.

title: Metal Wire Structure — Wire Spiral Pendant
body: Public edition. Public craft reference. A flat spiral pendant. Materials: 18-gauge copper wire, round-nose pliers, flush cutters, a mandrel (pen barrel). Steps: (1) cut 18 inches of wire; (2) make a tiny loop at one end; (3) wrap the wire around the mandrel in a flat coil; (4) slide off and tighten the coil; (5) form the outer tail into a bail loop. Tip: keep coils touching — gaps make the pendant look messy.

title: Metal Wire Structure — Wire Mesh Basket
body: Public edition. Public craft reference. A woven wire basket. Materials: 16-gauge steel wire for ribs, 20-gauge for weaving, pliers. Steps: (1) cut 8 rib wires and cross them at the center; (2) bind the center with weaving wire; (3) bend ribs upward into a bowl; (4) weave the 20-gauge wire over-under around the ribs, spiraling up; (5) fold rib tips inward to lock. Tip: keep the weave snug — loose weaving collapses when loaded.

title: Metal Wire Structure — Wire Plant Trellis
body: Public edition. Public craft reference. A fan trellis for climbing plants. Materials: 9-gauge galvanized steel wire (stiff), 14-gauge for ties, pliers, bolt cutters. Steps: (1) cut 7 verticals, longest in the middle; (2) cut 5 horizontals; (3) lash crossings with 14-gauge ties; (4) splay the bottom wires into ground stakes; (5) push into soil and check it stands in wind. Tip: galvanized wire survives weather — bare steel rusts in one season.

title: Metal Wire Structure — Wire Cube Frame
body: Public edition. Public craft reference. A geometric wire cube. Materials: 14-gauge steel or aluminum wire, pliers, a jig block. Steps: (1) cut 12 equal edges; (2) form the bottom square, twisting corners; (3) add 4 verticals; (4) form the top square; (5) square every corner against the jig. Tip: equal edges are everything — measure twice, cut once.

title: Metal Wire Structure — Wire Word Sculpture
body: Public edition. Public craft reference. A name or word bent from one continuous wire. Materials: 12-gauge aluminum wire, round-nose pliers, printed word template. Steps: (1) print the word large; (2) start at one end and bend along the template, making loops for letters like e and o; (3) keep the wire in one plane; (4) form a base foot at both ends; (5) stand and adjust. Tip: cursive-style connections keep it one continuous piece.

title: Metal Wire Structure — Wire Gauge and Strength Basics
body: Public edition. Public craft reference. Choosing wire: lower gauge numbers mean thicker wire — 9-gauge holds a trellis, 12-gauge holds a sculpture armature, 16-gauge bends easily for branches, 20-gauge is for weaving and wrapping. Aluminum is soft and rust-proof for sculpture; steel is stiff for structure; copper is beautiful for jewelry. Rule: pick the thickest wire you can still bend comfortably — thin wire fatigues and snaps where it is worked repeatedly.
capabilities: Choose aluminum vs steel vs copper
